conditioned_on: completion-pi-half-turn proved at explicitly operator-accepted mixed verification level
operational-unitary-half-turn freshly assembled at accepted mixed identification level
operational-spectral-whole-return-certificate accepted at additional mixed semantic correspondence level
update_policy: Condition the existing truth model on accepted pi closure and fresh operational regularity closure; omit resolved actions but retain old estimates as history. The same-phase flow record is now freshly assembled and its action is also removed. Full half-turn assembly is also freshly complete at the accepted identification level; its action is removed while earlier +- receipts remain historical. Whole-return is now accepted at its additional mixed semantic correspondence level; the portfolio is terminal and has no executable proof actions. Retain the historical estimates without rewriting forecasts. No new effort measurement or attempt-budget reset is asserted. The 24-EU calculation is a retained planning scenario, not a remaining-budget claim.
effort_unit: One focused proof/edit/check work cycle, not a minute of elapsed time. A long kernel rebuild need not be many effort units.
cost_scope: Marginal cost of one bounded attempt. Proof costs for dependent nodes apply after prerequisite certificates exist; they exclude prerequisite costs. Ranges are judgment ranges, not statistical confidence intervals.

objective.negative_target_outcome: Resolves the target negatively but is not rewarded as a positive certificate by this objective.
objective.secondary_diagnostic: Expected claim, target and joint information per effort for each direction; not the closure objective.

attempt_policy.failure_semantics: +- and -- leave the proposition unresolved. A failed proof cannot supply a prerequisite certificate.
attempt_policy.retry_policy: After an actual attempt, record the observation and replan explicitly. Do not silently repeat exhausted actions.
attempt_policy.conditional_independence: Distinct bounded-attempt outcomes are assumed independent conditional on the joint truth world. Flow rejection is the same experiment as regularity rejection and is not duplicated.
attempt_policy.soundness: P(++|false)=0 and P(-+|true)=0. These are proof/rejection outcomes, not polarity arrows.
attempt_policy.history: This is a new forward portfolio after the norm proof, not a restart of the predecessor's stopped source-contract audit. Priors summarize current judgment rather than a numerical update of that old prior.

joint_model.factorization: Pi and all-scale regularity are initially independent. Pi-scale regularity is certain when all-scale regularity holds, otherwise 0.40. Flow equals all-scale regularity because norm is proved. Half-turn equals pi-endpoints AND pi-scale regularity. The target conditional is 0.96 or 0.25 according to half-turn truth.
joint_model.scope_boundary: The final target is not equated with this particular proof route. The nonzero target probability after half-turn failure allows alternative implementation routes; no automatic parent-refutation edge is introduced.
joint_model.basis: The standard theorem and completed norm implementation make correctness highly plausible. Remaining uncertainty concerns the exact operational calculus and certificate contract. These probabilities are judgments, not measured frequencies.

completion-pi-half-turn.proof_use: Supplies the identified pi and exact endpoint certificate needed by the half-turn.
completion-pi-half-turn.rejection_use: Refutes the stated endpoint contract and blocks this constructive route, without automatically refuting every implementation.
completion-pi-half-turn.basis: Requires a constructive pi definition, identification with the reference pi and exact trigonometric half-turn laws; no ready endpoint package was found.

completion-phase-metric-regularity.proof_use: With norm already proved, enables the unit-circle-flow certificate.
completion-phase-metric-regularity.rejection_use: Locates a failure of the all-scale continuity/derivative contract. It need not fail at pi.
completion-phase-metric-regularity.basis: Existing operational Taylor bounds and comparison machinery can be reused, but metric differentiation and its transfer still need a precise implementation.

completion-unit-circle-flow.proof_use: Assembles the norm and regularity proofs for the same phase; supplies the half-turn flow input.
completion-unit-circle-flow.rejection_use: Since norm is proved, this is the regularity rejection test, not independent evidence.
completion-unit-circle-flow.basis: Expected record/transport assembly after prerequisites. The proposition is then known, but a checked certificate still has to be constructed.

operational-unitary-half-turn.proof_use: Specializes the same phase to the identified pi and enables whole-return assembly.
operational-unitary-half-turn.rejection_use: Rules out the specified operational half-turn, not every possible completion implementation.
operational-unitary-half-turn.basis: Expected specialization and endpoint assembly once flow and pi certificates are available. A direct disproof is substantially harder than failure to assemble them.

operational-spectral-whole-return-certif.proof_use: Closes the positive objective and makes the operational certificate exportable.
operational-spectral-whole-return-certif.rejection_use: Resolves the target negatively. Failure of a single candidate or proof attempt is insufficient.
operational-spectral-whole-return-certif.basis: Requires tensor/operator algebra, metric interval/gluing, piecewise generators, faithfulness and correspondence to the imported witness. Global nonexistence is much harder to certify than a candidate defect.

sensitivity.meaning: 27 scenarios vary the two open analytic proof costs and their conditional proof-completion probabilities. This is a sensitivity test, not a calibration claim.
